run_metadata.coverage_summary: Degraded, SEARCH-ONLY run (2026-11-20). The hard egress block seen on all recent runs persists and was re-tested this run: WebFetch to https://www.tenders.gov.au/atm, https://www.tenders.nsw.gov.au, https://www.tenders.vic.gov.au/tenders/open, https://www.tenders.act.gov.au/tenders/open and https://www.vendorpanel.com.au/publictenders.aspx all returned DNS ENOTFOUND, so no buyer-originated detail page, feed/API or tender document could be opened. Discovery was limited to WebSearch (US-indexed, lagging the 2026-11-20 run date, returning mostly cached snapshots and third-party aggregator pages). Tier 1 swept by search (AusTender; NSW buy.nsw/eTendering; VIC Buying for Victoria; QLD QTenders->VendorPanel/supply.qld.gov.au and Qld Health; WA Tenders WA/regional development-commission bulletins; SA Tenders SA; NT QTOL; ACT Tenders). Tier 2 swept by search (local government incl. Brisbane City Council; water corporations Sydney Water, Melbourne Water, Power and Water NT; electricity networks/generators incl. Territory Generation, Endeavour Energy; universities). Tier 3 MANDATORY check done by search (SAP Ariba Discovery / SAP Business Network Discovery, BHP GCMS, Rio Tinto Ariba, EstimateOne) - every corporate channel remained registration-gated or invitation-only with no publicly-visible open RFx; recorded as portals only, none fabricated. Net result this run: NO genuinely new buyer-originated opportunity could be confirmed to the routine's evidence bar. All 7 opportunities are carried from prior runs and remain within their open windows. Four were re-corroborated this run via buyer-page snapshots / trade press (DFAT-1113 PNG Health ENABLE REOI closing 1 Dec 2026; NSW ~$80M Master Media RFT closing 27 Nov 2026, re-confirmed by B&T 10 Nov + Mediaweek; Brisbane City Council Gardner Road Doc115483155 closing 7 Dec 2026 12 noon and Prebble Street Bikeway Doc118000917 still listed on the BCC current-tenders page). Three were carried forward within their open window but NOT independently re-corroborated this run (TfNSW New England Hwy Maitland Westbound ROI 26.0000139291.0941.ROI closing 11 Dec; Tenders ACT SL20260630 closing 1 Dec and PIMA0014211 closing 3 Dec). IMPORTANT HONESTY NOTE: an initial WebSearch summary of the NT QTOL portal appeared to list six December-closing NT tenders (T26-1304 fire detection; NTG25-0313 Alice Springs Hospital plumbing; NTG26-0127 aerial photography/LiDAR; AGC26-0097 vehicle rental; RFT0763 Power & Water incident management; CIDC020-26 Territory Generation Channel Island synchronous condenser). A targeted follow-up search showed the fire-detection and aerial/LiDAR items are actually Forward-Tender-Outlook (future, un-released) entries and that the specific IDs/close dates could not be re-corroborated (the condenser project's confirmed tender is the earlier CIO044-24A, already at respondent stage). These six were therefore treated as an unreliable search summary and were NOT captured as tenders (no fabrication of IDs, dates or scope). All 7 captured tenders remain headline-only and UNVERIFIED on an opened buyer page. No opportunity, deliverable, date, value or contact was fabricated.
gaps: HARD EGRESS BLOCK (unchanged, re-tested this run): all direct HTTPS to tender hosts is denied by the session network policy. WebFetch to www.tenders.gov.au, www.tenders.nsw.gov.au, www.tenders.vic.gov.au, www.tenders.act.gov.au and www.vendorpanel.com.au all returned DNS ENOTFOUND, so no buyer-originated detail page, feed/API or tender document could be opened. To restore full discovery these hosts should be allowed in the session network settings: www.tenders.gov.au, buy.nsw.gov.au, www.tenders.nsw.gov.au, www.tenders.vic.gov.au, qtenders.hpw.qld.gov.au / supply.qld.gov.au, www.tenders.wa.gov.au, www.tenders.sa.gov.au, www.tenders.tas.gov.au, tendersonline.nt.gov.au, www.tenders.act.gov.au, www.vendorpanel.com.au, service.ariba.com, gateway.icn.org.au, www.brisbane.qld.gov.au, www.sydneywater.com.au, www.melbournewater.com.au, www.endeavourenergy.com.au, estimateone.com, and individual council/university/utility/corporate sites.

Every tender captured this run is headline-only and UNVERIFIED on the buyer's own opened page. Titles, reference numbers and closing dates come from WebSearch snapshots of buyer pages, trade press and aggregators, not from an opened buyer detail page or an opened ATM. Deliverables, requirements, eligibility, evaluation criteria, submission mechanics, value and contacts are therefore mostly null and still need a detail pass once egress is restored.

NO genuinely new opportunity was captured this run. The most promising lead (a WebSearch summary claiming six December-closing NT QTOL tenders: T26-1304, NTG25-0313, NTG26-0127, AGC26-0097, RFT0763, CIDC020-26) did NOT survive verification: a follow-up search showed the fire-detection and aerial-photography/LiDAR items are Forward-Tender-Outlook (future/un-released) entries rather than open tenders, the stated close dates could not be re-corroborated, and the Channel Island synchronous-condenser tender that is confirmed is the earlier CIO044-24A (already at respondent stage), not CIDC020-26. To avoid fabricating IDs/dates/scope these were excluded from `tenders` and are noted here instead. The NT QTOL portal clearly has many active 'Details' tender records (e.g. T26-11xx/12xx series, NTG26-00xx, RFT04xx) that could not be opened or date-verified this run (egress block).

WebSearch index lags the run date (2026-11-20) and is US-indexed. Many surfaced notices had already closed (e.g. WA vessel 7403 'Cervantes' RFT DTMI416126 closed 17 Nov; QLD Corinda State High School science centre closed 19 Nov; NSW Crime Commission ICT managed services RFT-2013139 closed 8 May; numerous NT civil tenders closed early-mid Nov) and were correctly excluded, NOT captured. Genuinely recent (last 24-48h) buyer-originated notices are almost certainly undercounted.

Three carried opportunities were NOT independently re-corroborated this run and are asserted only as still within their open window: TfNSW New England Hwy Maitland Westbound ROI (26.0000139291.0941.ROI, closing 11 Dec) and the two Tenders ACT entries (SL20260630 closing 1 Dec; PIMA0014211 closing 3 Dec). The ACT listing snapshots have previously shown garbled/conflicting dates (one search this run suggested SL20260630 closes 3 Dec rather than 1 Dec), so ACT close dates and the PIMA0014211 procurement_type need confirmation on the live portal once egress is restored.

Foreshadowed / early-stage items seen only in portal-outlook, aggregator or news summaries and therefore NOT captured as tenders, pending release and verification on the buyer's own portal: NT fire-detection servicing and aerial-photography/LiDAR packages (Forward Tender Outlook, release windows mid/late 2026); Territory Generation Channel Island Power Station C1 synchronous condenser (project in detailed design; confirmed tender CIO044-24A at respondent stage); Melbourne Water WTP Preliminary Treatment Stage 1 and Field Services Panel renewal RFT (Zycus); University of Notre Dame Australia Managed SOC Services RFT (seen on its procurement page, dates unverified).

Tier 3 corporate (SAP Ariba Discovery / SAP Business Network Discovery, BHP GCMS, Rio Tinto Ariba, EstimateOne subcontractor packages, and major retail/bank/telco/energy e-sourcing hubs) remained registration-gated or invitation-only; no authenticated supplier session is available, so no corporate opportunity could be read. Recorded as portals only; no corporate tender fabricated. Management-consultancy / invitation-only RFPs are out of scope by definition and were not invented.

Source discovery was attempted this run (searches for new/rebranded portals, new corporate buyers, and sibling buyers on shared e-sourcing platforms) but surfaced only sources already in the routine's known set (e.g. AusTender Supplier Portal, GovWatch AU, VendorPanel, TenderLink) or non-buyer aggregators (projectory.com.au, globaltenders.com, openopps.com, starbridge.ai). new_sources_found = 0 this run.

Verify the University of Notre Dame Australia Managed Security Operations Centre (SOC) Services RFT on its procurement page (https://www.notredame.edu.au/staff/support/finance/procurement/suppliers) - seen via search but dates/status unconfirmed; capture as a tender once verified.

Once egress is restored, open the buyer detail pages for all seven carried opportunities and complete the deliverables/requirements detail pass: AusTender ATM for DFAT-1113 (PNG Health ENABLE); buy.nsw for the NSW Master Media RFT and TfNSW 26.0000139291.0941.ROI; Brisbane City Council Doc115483155 and Doc118000917; Tenders ACT SL20260630 and PIMA0014211 (resolve the ACT close-date conflict).
Keep the NT QTOL Forward Tender Outlook (DetailsFTO) feature on the weekly rotation as an early-warning channel for upcoming NT releases (fire-detection servicing, aerial photography/LiDAR, etc.).

tenders.title: PNG Health Program - Enhanced National Advice, Bilateral partnership, and Learning and Evidence (ENABLE) - Managing Contractor
tenders.buyer: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT)
tenders.category: Managing contractor services - international development / health systems
tenders.description: DFAT Request for Expressions of Interest to appoint a Managing Contractor for the PNG Health Program 'ENABLE' (Enhanced National Advice, Bilateral partnership, and Learning and Evidence), a new Australian health investment in Papua New Guinea expected to commence in 2027 for an initial five-year term. The REOI stage is to establish a shortlist of capable organisations, which would then be invited to a subsequent request-for-tender stage.
tenders.deliverables_summary: Per DFAT's public concept note, the Managing Contractor would deliver selected national-level enabling functions and strategic partnerships that support Australia's broader health portfolio in PNG and integrated primary health care - aligning national policy, financing, evidence and partnership functions with Australia's health investments under the PNG-Australia Health Partnership Strategy, and supporting delivery of quality health services including disease-outbreak containment. (Drawn from DFAT's published concept note read via search; full deliverables to be confirmed on the opened ATM.)
tenders.scope_of_work: ENABLE is positioned as delivering national enabling functions (policy, financing, evidence/learning, and partnership/coordination) and strategic partnerships supporting the PNG-Australia Health Partnership Strategy and integrated primary health care, delivered through a managing contractor over an initial five-year term from 2027. Full scope to be confirmed from the ATM documents.
tenders.eligibility: Open REOI to establish a shortlist of capable organisations able to deliver the program (not verified on the opened ATM this run).
tenders.contract_term: Initial five-year term (program expected to commence 2027), per DFAT concept note
tenders.closing_time: 10:00 AM ACT time (per aggregator snapshot; not verified on ATM)
tenders.submission_method: Lodge via AusTender (not verified on the opened ATM this run)
tenders.reasoning: Carryover (first seen 2026-11-19) re-corroborated this run (2026-11-20) via WebSearch of DFAT's own business-notification/concept-note pages (dfat.gov.au), which continue to show the PNG Health Program ENABLE managing-contractor REOI (ref DFAT-1113) released on AusTender and closing 1 December 2026. Buyer-originated Commonwealth channel (DFAT via AusTender); the AusTender ATM itself could not be opened due to the persistent egress block.
tenders.notes: HEADLINE-ONLY and UNVERIFIED on the opened ATM. Reference (DFAT-1113), publish (~5 Nov 2026) and close (1 Dec 2026, 10:00am ACT) come from DFAT's own pages plus an aggregator snapshot, not an opened AusTender record. Scope/deliverables text is from DFAT's public concept note read via search snippet; evaluation criteria, documents, value and contacts still null and need a detail pass once egress is restored. Re-corroborated as still open this run (2026-11-20).
